title: Normalizing Flows: Change of Variables, Intuitively
creator: Danilo Rezende
summary: An intuitive walk through invertible maps, the change-of-variables formula, and affine coupling layers.
contentText:
# Normalizing Flows: Change of Variables, Intuitively

A normalizing flow turns a simple base density into a complex one through an invertible map x = f(z). Because the map is invertible, we can evaluate the exact likelihood of any data point.

## The change-of-variables formula

Taking logs turns the product into a sum, which is what we actually optimize. The whole art is choosing f so the Jacobian determinant is cheap to compute.

- Split the input into two halves.
- Transform one half, conditioned on the other.
- Stack many layers, alternating which half is held fixed.
readerHTML:
A normalizing flow turns a simple base density into a complex one through an invertible, differentiable map \( x = f(z) \). Because the map is invertible, we can evaluate the exact likelihood of any data point — no lower bound, no sampling.

The change-of-variables formula

If \( z \sim p_Z \) and \( x = f(z) \), the density of \( x \) follows from conservation of probability mass:

\[ p_X(x) = p_Z\!\left(f^{-1}(x)\right)\,\left|\det \frac{\partial f^{-1}(x)}{\partial x}\right| \]

Taking logs turns the product into a sum, which is what we actually optimize:

\[ \log p_X(x) = \log p_Z\!\left(f^{-1}(x)\right) + \log\left|\det J_{f^{-1}}(x)\right| \]
The entire art is choosing \( f \) so the Jacobian determinant is cheap to compute — ideally triangular, so the determinant is just the product of the diagonal.

A minimal coupling layer

Affine coupling keeps half the dimensions fixed and uses them to parameterize an affine transform of the other half:

def coupling(x, mask, net):
    x_a = x * mask
    s, t = net(x_a)            # scale and shift
    return x_a + (1 - mask) * (x * exp(s) + t)
  • Split the input into two halves.
  • Transform one half, conditioned on the other.
  • Stack many layers, alternating which half is held fixed.

The log-determinant is then simply \( \sum_i s_i \), and inversion is exact and in closed form.

title: karpathy/nanoGPT
creator: Andrej Karpathy
summary: The simplest, fastest repository for training/finetuning medium-sized GPTs.
contentText:
# karpathy/nanoGPT

The simplest, fastest repository for training/finetuning medium-sized GPTs. It is a rewrite of minGPT that prioritizes teeth over education.

## install

- torch, numpy, transformers, datasets, tiktoken, wandb, tqdm

## quick start

Train a character-level GPT on the works of Shakespeare. First download a tiny dataset and encode it. Then train a baby GPT with a small network. On one GPU this trains in a few minutes.

The code itself is plain and readable: train.py is a ~300-line boilerplate training loop and model.py defines the GPT model definition.

title: The Power of Small Wins
creator: Teresa Amabile & Steven Kramer
summary: Progress in meaningful work is the strongest daily motivator.
contentText:
# The Power of Small Wins

## What really motivates people at work

Of all the things that can boost emotions, motivation, and perceptions during a workday, the single most important is making progress in meaningful work. And the more frequently people experience that sense of progress, the more likely they are to be creatively productive in the long run.

## The progress principle

If a person is motivated and happy at the end of the workday, it's a good bet that he or she made some progress. If the person drags out of the office disengaged and joyless, a setback is most likely to blame.

- Setbacks loom larger than progress for many managers.
- Small wins compound: minor milestones can produce outsized positive reactions.
- Protecting people's inner work life is a manager's most leverage-laden job.

## What managers can do

Scrupulously avoid impeding progress by changing goals autocratically, being indecisive, or holding up resources. Catalysts and nourishers — clear goals, autonomy, help, and respect — keep the engine running.

title: A Quiet Reading Setup
creator: Ink & Margin
summary: What makes a reading view comfortable.
note:
Borrow the 60–75 char measure for the iOS reader.

Follow up: test the serif at 18pt vs 19pt.
readerHTML:
A good reading setup disappears. The page is wide enough to hold a comfortable line length, the type is set in a serif that does not fight the eye, and the chrome stays out of the way until you reach for it.

Three rules

  • Measure around 60–75 characters per line.
  • Set body text at a size you'd choose for a paperback, not a billboard.
  • Let the background follow the system — paper by day, ink by night.

Everything else is decoration.

title: On Attention and Reading
creator: The Long Read
contentText:
# On Attention and Reading

A conversation about how the medium shapes comprehension: why long-form reading on a calm screen beats an endless feed, and how a reader mode that strips clutter can restore the kind of sustained attention that deep reading needs.

Topics: the economics of distraction, reader modes, e-ink versus LCD, and building tools that respect focus.
